negative_findings.description: No named authorised Ingenico, Verifone or PAX distributor for North Macedonia was identified.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal supply attribution for the MK POS estate is currently unresolved; the estate is probably supplied through the acquirers/processors (CaSys, Payten) rather than a visible retail distributor.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: That register would be the single best enumeration of merchant-side hardware suppliers and their market shares; without it the merchant-terminal supplier map has to be assembled firm by firm.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no IAD layer exists in MK, published ATM counts can be read as bank-owned estate; that assumption should be verified before modelling.

negative_findings.description: No procurement-portal route to MK bank ATM/POS tenders was found; MK commercial banks are private and do not tender through e-nabavki.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: the supplier side (vendor references, trade press, cash-firm profiles) is the only practical route to procurement-level intelligence in MK.

brief: North Macedonia's ATM/POS technology supply is a short, concentrated chain: global OEMs (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Ingenico, Verifone, PAX) do not appear directly in the market and instead reach banks through regional channel players - Printec (present since 2006, ATM supply and maintenance, Komercijalna Banka named as a reference) and the Asseco SEE / Payten group in Skopje (core banking, cards, ATM/POS services and outsourcing) - while CaSys AD Skopje, the domestic certified card processor, actually runs the ATM and POS networks and card personalisation for the banks and is therefore the single richest vendor-side source. Because MK commercial banks are private and tender nothing publicly, the usable intelligence sits in vendor country pages and case studies, Asseco group segment reporting, listed-bank investor presentations, and the small MK trade/business press (it.mk, ecommerce.mk, faktor.mk) that covers payment launches and payments-industry ownership. A parallel cash-side cluster - Nikob's regional cash-processing centre, Perpetum Mobile's daily-takings transfer service, and NLB's own commercial cash centre - is the best indirect read on cash intensity and on banks outsourcing cash handling. The main unresolved holes are the POS hardware import/distributor tier, the absence of a published UJP register of approved fiscal-device suppliers, and no company-registry or Albanian-language coverage yet.
